xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4652: Fly VMs as machines: pan serve on the VM, linked at spawn

plan.title: Fly VMs as machines: pan serve on the VM, linked at spawn
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: W-FLY2's Done-when (a conversation started on Fly streams home with a fly-<id> chip and is pulled home) needs image, VM provisioning, the channel route parameter, the VM gate mode, linking, the conversation door and the spend loops together; none is observable alone. The separable part (work agents, PAN-1775) is already split to PAN-4734. Files are exact and items are vertical; the surface spans src/lib, src/cli, src/dashboard, docker, tests and four doc trees.

narratives.Problem: FR-18/D-12 make a Fly VM an ordinary linked machine, but the pan-workspace image has no pan, Fly VMs expose no port, the channel client cannot pin one machine behind <app>.fly.dev, a VM would label itself with its bare machine id, the heartbeat/credential/cap loops only see VMs with remote-state.json, and home cannot start a conversation on a linked machine.
narratives.Proposal: Ship pan and Docker in the image; add a Fly machine service (mirroring SSH machines) that creates a VM with a 443 tls/http service, pins pan --version to home's, writes a fly-<machineId> identity, syncs credentials, starts `pan serve --no-open` detached in public-link-only mode with the tmux backend, arms the PAN-4295 watchdog, reads a pairing code from `pan pair --json` over Machines exec and links one way over wss://<app>.fly.dev/ws/link?fly-instance=<id>. With --project it clones and registers the project on the VM; with --message it starts a Claude Code conversation there through the link. Unlink destroys the VM; the deacon child heartbeats, refreshes credentials and destroys stopped or idle Fly machines; the cap counts them. `pan machines add-fly` and POST /api/machines/fly are the door #4651 and #4638 build on. A live, operator-consented checkpoint proves the chip, Pull here and Docker (OD-4).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Moving `pan start --remote` work agents onto the linked path, session rows for them, and closing PAN-1775 — PAN-4734; this PR says `Refs #1775`, never `Closes #1775`
- The Machine field, Fly (new VM) in the new-conversation dialog, and `--machine fly` on pan start / pan worker run / pan lane start — #4651 (W-WORK1)
- Workers and gauntlet lanes placed on Fly machines and `gauntlet.fly.max_vms` — #4651 and #4638
- A new `docker` capability field or tags in the environment descriptor, and `--needs` placement — #4651 (W-WORK6, FR-23)
- Codex or any harness other than Claude Code on a Fly machine — #4296
- Joining Fly VMs to the tailnet — #1254
- A dashboard UI button to add a Fly machine
- Restarting a stopped Fly machine (rootfs resets; it is destroyed instead)
- Durable-tier volumes for Fly machines
- GitLab-hosted projects on a Fly machine
- Automatic allocation of the Fly app's public IPs
- Any change to the remote work-agent spawn, reap, tell or kill paths beyond the FR-12 cap count
- Changing the image CMD or the build-workspace-image CI workflow
- Copying any operator SSH private key to a VM

autoDecisions.summary: The VM issues the pairing code via `pan pair --json` over Machines exec; home links (D-1)
autoDecisions.rationale: Codes exist only in the issuing server's memory and no import path exists; the SSH-machine flow already does this and keeps the code off the network route being paired.

autoDecisions.summary: Split the work-agent conversion and the PAN-1775 closure into PAN-4734 (D-15)
autoDecisions.rationale: It rewrites the reap/tell/kill contract PAN-4295 restored and live-tested today and would double this PR; the W-FLY2 Done-when tests a conversation, which this plan delivers.

autoDecisions.summary: Public route is wss://<app>.fly.dev/ws/link with a fly-instance parameter lifted into the fly-force-instance-id header (D-3)
autoDecisions.rationale: Machines in an app share <app>.fly.dev; raw TCP cannot be pinned to a machine and needs a dedicated IPv4; /ws/link already exists for TLS-terminating proxies.

autoDecisions.summary: OD-4 fallback adds no descriptor field; the docker tag belongs to #4651 W-WORK6 (D-8)
autoDecisions.rationale: FR-23 assigns docker detection (`docker info` succeeds) and --needs placement to #4651; a second field here would conflict with it.

autoDecisions.summary: Version equality by npm install at provisioning, not per-release image tags (D-7)
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids a CI workflow change (workflow pushes need SSH) and guarantees the SSH-machine equality rule; home's package version is always a published release.

autoDecisions.summary: Fly machines are destroyed, never stopped or restarted; idle after 30 min with no active linked conversation (D-9, FR-16)
autoDecisions.rationale: The rootfs resets on start, so a stopped machine is useless; FR-18 requires spend to be bounded.

autoDecisions.summary: `pan machines add-fly` + `POST /api/machines/fly` is this issue's door; --machine fly stays with #4651
autoDecisions.rationale: #4651's body says its Fly (new VM) choice and --machine fly need this issue; owning the flag here would collide with W-WORK1.

autoDecisions.summary: Public-link-only mode on the VM server (OVERDECK_PUBLIC_LINK_ONLY=1)
autoDecisions.rationale: The VM's port is on the public internet through Fly's proxy; only the /ws/link channel needs to be reachable from outside.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-4 (D-3). In `parseTransportUrl`, for a `wss:` URL whose `fly-instance` query parameter is non-empty, delete the parameter, and return `{ kind: 'wss', url: <url without it>, headers: { 'fly-force-instance-id': <value> } }`. In `connectTransport` dial `new WsClient(target.url, target.headers ? { headers: target.headers } : undefined)`. Export `FLY_INSTANCE_PARAM = 'fly-instance'`. Every other URL is dialled exactly as today.

OVERDECK_PUBLIC_LINK_ONLY makes the gate refuse non-channel remote requests

narrative.Action: PRD WI-5. Add rule 0b after the Funnel rule (header comment and code): when `OVERDECK_PUBLIC_LINK_ONLY === '1'` (read through a `publicLinkOnly(env = process.env)` helper) and the request is neither a channel request (`channelOfRequest`) nor a trusted local caller (loopback peer without a proxy forwarding header, the rule-4 test), respond 404 `{ "error": "not_found" }` for every path, including the static SPA. The `/ws/link` upgrade is handled before the gate and is unaffected.

narrative.Action: PRD WI-11. heartbeatFlyMachines writes the host heartbeat by exec per record (non-zero exit = failure line). sweepFlyMachines removes a record when getMachine shows stopped/destroyed/failed or 404 (API errors = skip), or when no linked_conversations row for its environmentId is active — releasedTo null AND (row.status === 'active' OR row.lastActivityAt within the idle window) — for at least `[remote.fly] machine_idle_minutes` (default 30, 0 disables; idle-since kept in memory), or when linkId is null for 30 min. Remove = destroyFlyVm + removeLink + removeFlyMachine + one cloister activity entry. Zero records ⇒ return [] before constructing any client. Register both in startHygieneScheduler at REMOTE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS, not behind the freeze. Add `machine_idle_minutes?: number` to RemoteFlyConfig.

Given a record whose only linked conversation is unreleased but has status `ended` and lastActivityAt older than the window, when 29 minutes pass under fake timers, then it is kept, and at 30 minutes it is removed; a row with status `active` in between resets the timer
